transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-03-30
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Bluehaven Head of Procurement), Samir Patel (Bluehaven SecOps), Evan Li (Bluehaven Eng Manager), Hannah Gray (Bluehaven Legal)

Summary:
Quick kickoff between procurement, security, legal and Redwood to validate commercial path (PO, billing), legal docs (MSA/DPA exceptions), and technical preflight for a 3-month pilot on dedicated capacity with KMS integration and EU data residency constraints. Customer requested pricing path, egress cost clarity, and audit log retention. Actionable next steps and owners agreed at end.

Topics covered:
- MSA redlines and DPA exceptions (data residency, auditability)
- Billing / PO and invoice terms, escrow/escrow-like asks
- SLA thresholds for pilot and roll to prod
- KMS/HSM integration and key custody options
- Network connectivity: VPC peering vs PrivateLink
- Pilot sizing, benchmarks, and cost model (committed vs usage)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, um i'm alex i'll be your account lead for this track. quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Maya Ortiz: maya here, procurement.
[00:00:11] Samir Patel: samir, security.
[00:00:13] Evan Li: evan, eng.
[00:00:15] Hannah Gray: hannah, legal.
[00:00:18] Priya Nair: priya from redwood se team, hi.

[00:01:02] Alex Chen: cool thanks. high level goal for today is to align on the commercial path - do you want a PO, invoice net45, or commit? and second, legal questions on the msa/dpa and any immediate blockers for kms/peering.
[00:01:28] Maya Ortiz: short answer is we prefer PO + net45 invoices, procurement needs to own that. we'll review commits but pilot should be low friction.
[00:01:41] Hannah Gray: on legal, we'll need to look at the dpa and check residency. also need to understand audit logs retention and right to audit.

[00:02:10] Priya Nair: technically we support three deployment modes, hosted api, dedicated GPU pool, or private/vpc. for your pilot we described dedicated pool with vpc peering + customer-managed keys via kms. note: key custody options: bring-your-own-kms (BYOK) with customer-managed keys in your cloud ksm or we can integrate with HSM, caveats on egress.
[00:02:40] Samir Patel: when you say integrate kms, do you mean keys never leave our control? we need to know whether private keys are wrapped by redwood or kept entirely in our ksm.
[00:02:56] Priya Nair: good q. we offer two patterns: BYOK (keys stay in your cloud kms and are used for envelope encryption) or an HSM-backed integration where keys remain under your tenancy and we only get wrapped tokens. there are perf impacts for some operations if you require frequent decrypt calls.

[00:03:35] Evan Li: perf impacts meaning increased latency per request? can you quantify?
[00:03:41] Priya Nair: yeah, envelope-decrypt on every token streaming can add 10-30ms per request depending on region and kms latency. we have caching of wrapped keys in the runtime to reduce calls, but for very high qps you may want a dedicated pool in eu-west with local kms.

[00:04:20] Alex Chen: also to call out pricing tradeoffs—dedicated pools are committed monthly and have a different rate structure than hosted per-token. for pilots we can do a reduced pilot rate + a commitment credit.

[00:04:45] Maya Ortiz: okay procurement wise we'll need a written pilot price and the msadpa redlines. we also have a compliance playbook that requires soc2 type ii and a vendor assessment.

[00:05:05] Priya Nair: we will include SOC2, ISO27001, and the latest pen test summary. we can also share a short architecture diagram for the vpc peer and kms hops.

[00:05:30] Hannah Gray: two legal asks: one, we typically request 12 month log retention for auditability; two, we want a clause to limit data export to EU nodes only for eu customers — is that supported?
[00:05:47] Priya Nair: data residency via region pinning is supported in dedicated and private modes. for hosted you can restrict to eu regions but we need to confirm cross-region fallbacks. log retention can be extended as a paid add-on; default retention is 90 days, we can do 12 months under a separate agreement.

[00:06:20] Samir Patel: how about keys in flight and at rest? encryption at rest is standard but we need to ensure audit logs are tamper-evident and accessible to us on request.
[00:06:33] Priya Nair: logs are cryptographically signed and stored in our audit pipeline; for dedicated/private customers we can push logs to your s3 or splunk via secure channel. there may be small egress costs for that.

[00:07:00] Evan Li: what's the egress model? we need clarity because finance flags egress as a surprise cost.
[00:07:07] Alex Chen: good point. we typically only charge for network egress when pushing large artifacts; audit log push is metered—small for logs, larger for model snapshots or cache transfers. we'll send a spreadsheet with sample egress scenarios.

[00:07:38] Maya Ortiz: pricing approval will need an internal cost model: pilot flat fee, expected cc per month, plus egress estimates. can you provide a sample pricing breakdown?
[00:07:47] Alex Chen: yes, we'll provide a pilot quote: pilot fee + reduced per-token rates during the pilot + optional committed discount. we can try to structure as a one-time pilot credit applied to future committed spend.

[00:08:20] Priya Nair: on the technical side i want to flag the KMS handshake: if you require HSM-backed keys with no export, we'll likely need a short architecture change and a preflight test—this is standard but takes 2-3 weeks to validate for the pilot.

[00:08:45] Hannah Gray: timeline concern — our procurement window is tight; can legal and procurement review in parallel?
[00:08:52] Alex Chen: yes we normally run parallel review — procurement for PO & billing, legal for MSA/DPA. redwood can ingest redlines and propose responses quickly; target response within 5 business days for initial redline pass.

[00:09:30] Evan Li: for the pilot we want a simple SLA: 95th percentile tail latency under 350ms for inference on a 2k token window, and availability 99.5. is that realistic?
[00:09:47] Priya Nair: depends on model and qps; for dedicated pools we can tune to meet 350ms P95 for many open LLMs with optimized kernels and continuous batching, but we should run a benchmark with your workload to validate. availability 99.5 is achievable on dedicated with canary rollouts and fallback to hosted; if cross-region redundancy is required that changes architecture and cost.

[00:10:25] Samir Patel: fallback — you said you'd do automatic fallback to hosted variants. does that mean data could leave our region?
[00:10:33] Priya Nair: fallback can be constrained by policy — for strict residency we can disable cross-region fallback and instead auto-throttle or queue. tradeoff is availability vs residency guarantees.

[00:11:00] Alex Chen: just to document assumptions: pilot will run on a dedicated pool in eu-west; BYOK with customer's kms; audit logs pushed to customer's splunk; PO payment net45; legal to review msa/dpa with our standard redlines.

[00:11:22] Maya Ortiz: that matches internal ask. procurement needs to know billing entity — we operate via Bluehaven Holdings (billing). i'll send the billing entity details.

[00:11:40] Hannah Gray: payment terms — we prefer net30, but if net45 is required by the vendor team we can accept net45 with a 2% discount for net30. is that something we can negotiate?
[00:11:52] Alex Chen: we can hand that to our finance ops and see—usually net30 is standard but enterprise billing sometimes goes net45. we'll surface that and propose options in the quote.

[00:12:18] Evan Li: technical preflight — priya, what do you need from us to run a benchmark?
[00:12:23] Priya Nair: sample request distribution (tokens per request, concurrency), model variant you expect to use (open model name or Llama variant), expected peak qps, and any prompt engineering patterns that cause long context. also ip allowlist and test keys for the benchmark environment.

[00:12:45] Evan Li: i'll pull a 48-hour trace and a summary of 95/99 latency numbers and upload to the shared drive.

[00:13:02] Alex Chen: i'll open a support ticket to provision a pilot sandbox; priya will run the benchmark and share results in 72 hours after we have the trace.

[00:13:22] Priya Nair: note: some terminology in our docs is inconsistent—our product names sometimes transcribe as redwood dedict rather than redwood dedicated in the exported doc; ignore that.

[00:13:40] Maya Ortiz: hah yeah we saw that in the previous deck.

[00:14:10] Hannah Gray: on data residency in dpa: we may ask for a cross-border transfer clause and liability limits — is redwood open to negotiate caps on liability for data processing?
[00:14:24] Alex Chen: we typically have standard liability terms but for enterprise contracts we can discuss caps per negotiation; i'll flag legal.

[00:15:00] Samir Patel: security controls — do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning? we need RBAC to map teams and roles.
[00:15:10] Priya Nair: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported; RBAC is provided at the token and team level. enterprise zones can add stricter session timeouts.

[00:15:35] Evan Li: can we have a read-only audit view for our security team that can't be modified?
[00:15:40] Priya Nair: yes, we can provide read-only log pushes and role-limited dashboards; for dedicated customers we can export logs to your SIEM.

[00:16:05] Maya Ortiz: procurement also wanted to confirm insurance and subprocessor list for their vendor assessment.
[00:16:12] Alex Chen: we'll include our current insurance certificate and the subprocessor list.

[00:16:35] Hannah Gray: redlines workflow — we prefer to send a single consolidated set of DPA redlines. what's the manifest you prefer?
[00:16:43] Alex Chen: send consolidated redlines to alex@redwood.com; our legal will respond with a comment file. target turnaround 5 business days.

[00:17:10] Priya Nair: for the pilot SLA we should write the acceptance criteria in the SOW: dataset, test inputs, and target metrics (P95 latency, error rate). we'll draft the SOW and attach to the pilot PO.

[00:17:38] Evan Li: does redwood provide any cost guardrails or alerts during pilot to avoid surprise bills?
[00:17:44] Alex Chen: yes, we can set hard caps for spend and notifications. also token-level breakouts in console for daily usage.

[00:18:05] Samir Patel: how about data deletion and e-discovery — if we need a purge or legal hold, what's the process?
[00:18:13] Priya Nair: we support on-demand data purge and can provide a retention/hard-delete process; legal hold requests require a signed form and are logged; there's typically a small ops window to execute.

[00:18:45] Maya Ortiz: procurement question — is there any vendor escrow option for models or data?
[00:18:52] Alex Chen: we offer model snapshot escrow for an additional fee for customers that need to keep an offline copy; it's not common but it's an option.

[00:19:12] Hannah Gray: one more legal question — indemnity and IP clauses, specifically generated output ownership for customer prompts. we need it spelled out in the msa.
[00:19:24] Alex Chen: our standard tems grant customers ownership of customer-provided content and generated outputs for customer data. we'll confirm language in the MSA draft.

[00:20:05] Evan Li: great. i'd like to schedule the infra deep dive — two-hour slot for network, kms, and pilot runbook.
[00:20:12] Priya Nair: we can do 90-120 mins. i'll send 3 proposed windows after this call.

[00:20:35] Alex Chen: commercial: i'll include pilot pricing options: 1) 3-month pilot flat fee with X compute, 2) pay-as-you-go with safety cap, 3) committed monthly with credits.

[00:21:05] Maya Ortiz: procurement will need a line item for audit log export (s3 push) and for KMS integration validation. those extras need prices.

[00:21:30] Alex Chen: acknowledged; pricing spreadsheet will break out base pilot, audit log export egress estimate, kms integration labor, and optional model escrow fee.

[00:22:05] Hannah Gray: can redwood accept some DPA language where Bluehaven remains the data controller and redwood is the processor? that's our standard frame.
[00:22:17] Alex Chen: yes that's standard — DPA will reflect customer as controller, redwood as processor; any exceptions will be called out.

[00:22:50] Samir Patel: curious — any competitor-specific differentiators that would matter here? we've looked at some hosted vendors that don't support BYOK.
[00:22:59] Priya Nair: right — a big differentiator is our unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and explicit BYOK support plus audit log export and per-token cost breakdowns. some vendors force hosted only.

[00:23:25] Evan Li: ok that helps our assessment.

[00:23:50] Alex Chen: we're about halfway; any burning issues we haven't covered?
[00:23:56] Maya Ortiz: timeline— procurement wants to approve pilot within 2 weeks if legal signs off quickly.

[00:24:05] Hannah Gray: legal will aim for a first-pass redline within 4 business days.

[00:24:26] Priya Nair: tech note—for benchmarking we'll need ephemeral test keys; is that ok?
[00:24:31] Evan Li: yes we'll provide test keys and ip ranges.

[00:25:00] Alex Chen: ok logistically next steps: i will send the MSA/DPA + security pack by 2025-04-02; priya will provision the sandbox and run the benchmark after we receive the trace; bluehaven to send PO template and billing contact.

[00:25:20] Maya Ortiz: noted. procurement will coordinate internally.

[00:25:40] Hannah Gray: one question on liability limits: our counsel will propose cap equal to insurance limits; we can share suggested language.

[00:25:50] Alex Chen: understood, we'll review.

[00:26:10] Priya Nair: small technical caveat — if you pick a model that requires large kv cache disk, there is an initial cache warmup egress for first snapshot; we'll call that out in the SOW.

[00:26:36] Evan Li: thanks for flagging. we'll call out model family and expected context size in our trace.

[00:27:00] Alex Chen: quick recap before we break: action owners, deliverables, and dates—everyone agree?
[00:27:09] Maya Ortiz: yes.
[00:27:12] Evan Li: yes.
[00:27:15] Hannah Gray: yes.
[00:27:20] Priya Nair: yes.

[00:27:35] Alex Chen: ok we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pricing spreadsheet. any final q's?
[00:27:45] Samir Patel: none from me.

[00:28:00] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll check back in after legal redlines and the benchmark.

[00:28:10] Meeting ended

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word swap (redwood dedict/dedicate), transcription truncated punctuation in some sentences, speaker labels are accurate but may have been normalized by the exporter.
